messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text: Hianxo rises from the harbour in red lacquer and cedar roofs. The letter from Jiansho Academy has brought your party across the Jehopa Ocean for a tournament group entry, but it says little about who asked for you. At the foot of the gangplank a woman with three white tails waits with a careful bow and a smile, and her eyes have already found you.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Honami, who asked for us, and why us?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

messages.name: Dalan

*He follows closely, eyes scanning the crowds of students and their instructors as they pass. He's clearly nervous, his shoulders hunched slightly, and he seems to be trying to make himself small in the crowd.*

messages.text:
"You got it," *she says, and her grin is sharp.*

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text: "Welcome to Jiansho Academy! I'm Megumi Xianxu, Head of the Student Council." The smile is flawless; behind her back, her hands are wringing the spine of a register book. "And you must be Honami's... guests. How brave of you. Shall I read you the rules before you sign, or after?"

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The courtyard is full of students in training robes, their chatter filling the space, all eyes on the newcomers. A few of them are whispering, pointing. Megumi stands by a stone table where a long sheet of paper is laid out, the tournament register, and next to her is a ink-brush and a bottle of ink.
Behind her, the Academy's main building rises in tiers of grey tile and dark timber, its doors open to the training grounds. The sun is high, and the heat is starting to build.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
Students stop at the edges of the courtyard, whispering as the party passes. Some stare openly at the foreigners. Dalan's shoulders hunch lower and he grips the strap of his bow, while Belle's hand remains steady on the hilt of Cleaver.
Honami stops just before Megumi, her red eyes fixed on the other woman's face. One of her white tails twitches, brushing against Max Nightriver's robe as she leans in.
swipes:
The courtyard is full of students in training robes, their chatter filling the space, all eyes on the newcomers. A few of them are whispering, pointing. Megumi stands by a stone table where a long sheet of paper is laid out, the tournament register, and next to her is a ink-brush and a bottle of ink.
Behind her, the Academy's main building rises in tiers of grey tile and dark timber, its doors open to the training grounds. The sun is high, and the heat is starting to build.

Students stop at the edges of the courtyard, whispering as the party passes. Some stare openly at the foreigners. Dalan's shoulders hunch lower and he grips the strap of his bow, while Belle's hand remains steady on the hilt of Cleaver.
Honami stops just before Megumi, her red eyes fixed on the other woman's face. One of her white tails twitches, brushing against Max Nightriver's robe as she leans in.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We sign under Honami's name. Where do we fight?

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"Where you fight?" She smiles sweetly, her fingers trailing along the spine of the book. "That's quite simple. You fight in the tournament grounds, of course. The first round is fought in the sparring courtyards, which are just across the way."
*She points with a slender finger toward a section of the courtyard filled with training equipment and weapons racks.*
"The second round is fought in the central arena, and the final... as you've heard, is fought before the Emperor in the Imperial Palace."
*Her eyes flick toward Honami, and then back to Max Nightriver.*
"You'll find your first-round opponents and your opponents for each round listed on the notice board. It updates every day, so do keep an eye on it. Are there any other questions you have before we get started?"

messages.text: Show us the board, Honami. Who do we face in the first round?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:

*She scans the lists, her white tail swishing behind her as she points to a name on one of the scrolls.*

*She smiles and looks up at Max Nightriver with a red gaze, her eyes sparkling.*
"Shall I prepare a charm for you to use? Something to bolster your strength, perhaps?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Honami, who asked for us, and why us?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

"On it!" *Belle doesn't wait for a second word, and her axe is already moving. She spins in a wide, brutal circle, the head of Cleaver whistling through the air.*
*The big monk moves—a slow, calm sidestep that's almost mocking.* "Fuckin' patience," *she mutters under her breath, and her jaw sets.*
*She steps into the attack, her own weight behind the swing.* "You want to play it safe? Try this!" *she roars, and the axe comes down like a hammer, the sand erupting again in a storm of grey grit.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Honami, who asked for us, and why us?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text: "Welcome to Jiansho Academy! I'm Megumi Xianxu, Head of the Student Council." The smile is flawless; behind her back, her hands are wringing the spine of a register book. "And you must be Honami's... guests. How brave of you. Shall I read you the rules before you sign, or after?"

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
Students stop at the edges of the courtyard, whispering as the party passes. Some stare openly at the foreigners. Dalan's shoulders hunch lower and he grips the strap of his bow, while Belle's hand remains steady on the hilt of Cleaver.
Honami stops just before Megumi, her red eyes fixed on the other woman's face. One of her white tails twitches, brushing against Max Nightriver's robe as she leans in.
swipes:
The courtyard is full of students in training robes, their chatter filling the space, all eyes on the newcomers. A few of them are whispering, pointing. Megumi stands by a stone table where a long sheet of paper is laid out, the tournament register, and next to her is a ink-brush and a bottle of ink.
Behind her, the Academy's main building rises in tiers of grey tile and dark timber, its doors open to the training grounds. The sun is high, and the heat is starting to build.

Honami stops just before Megumi, her red eyes fixed on the other woman's face. One of her white tails twitches, brushing against Max Nightriver's robe as she leans in.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We sign under Honami's name. Where do we fight?

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"Where you fight?" She smiles sweetly, her fingers trailing along the spine of the book. "That's quite simple. You fight in the tournament grounds, of course. The first round is fought in the sparring courtyards, which are just across the way."
*She points with a slender finger toward a section of the courtyard filled with training equipment and weapons racks.*
"The second round is fought in the central arena, and the final... as you've heard, is fought before the Emperor in the Imperial Palace."
*Her eyes flick toward Honami, and then back to Max Nightriver.*
"You'll find your first-round opponents and your opponents for each round listed on the notice board. It updates every day, so do keep an eye on it. Are there any other questions you have before we get started?"

"Shall I prepare a charm for you to use? Something to bolster your strength, perhaps?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We signed the register, all three of us, so we're in. Belle, you take the first bout against Chen Wei.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"Huh? You want me to go first?" *Belle stops dead, her hand tightening on Cleaver's leather grip.* "You sure you don't want to let some fancy-pants cultivator show how it's done, Nightriver?"
*Her gaze flickers to Honami for a moment before settling back on Max, brown eyes searching. Then she laughs, a short, sharp sound.*
"Alright. If that's what you want." *She heaves her axe over her shoulder, the massive stone head catching the midday sun.* "I'll show this fire-shitter what happens when you try to burn a Mountain-born."
*She starts walking toward the sparring courts, each footfall heavy and deliberate.* "Don't go and lose your head while I'm having a bit of fun."

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
"Yes, Captain." *Dalan nods and scans the area, his green-hooded capelet fluttering as he weaves through the students.*
*He finds a clear spot on a raised stone ledge, far from the main crowd but with a perfect view of the fighting ring.* "Here, this is a good vantage point." *He says softly as he leads the party toward the ledge.*
*His eyes are already scanning the courtyard, taking in every detail—the students, the instructors, the sparring rings, the way the air feels just before a fight.* "I'll keep a lookout from here, and let you know if anything interesting happens."

messages.text:
*Belle stops at the edge of the sparring ring, her hand resting on Cleaver's grip.*
"Tch. Let's see if this Chen Wei can actually fight, or if he's just another pompous blowhard." *She spits on the ground and narrows her eyes at the students and instructors who gather around the ring.*
*She scans the crowd, looking for Chen Wei or any other student who looks like they could be worth her time.* "Anyone here gonna step up, or am I just gonna be standing around like a decorative pot?"
*The students whisper among themselves, their eyes wide as they take in the towering woman with the massive axe.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: I close the distance and drive my shoulder into the left monk's guard, trying to shove him toward the ring edge.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The left monk takes Max Nightriver's shoulder with a sharp exhale, feet skidding back through the raked sand. He doesn't go down; instead, he twists and grabs Max Nightriver's arm, the grip like iron. His eyes are empty, and he doesn't make a sound.
The right monk is already moving—a low, sweeping kick meant to catch Max Nightriver's ankle and throw them off balance. The big monk doesn't rush in, just watches with a calm that feels dangerous.
Belle's axe Cleaver comes down in a sudden, crushing arc. The sand erupts in a spray of stone-grey grit, and the sound is like a hammer meeting a wall.

messages.text: I close the distance and drive my shoulder into the left monk's guard, trying to shove him toward the ring edge.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The left monk takes Max Nightriver's shoulder with a sharp exhale, feet skidding back through the raked sand. He doesn't go down; instead, he twists and grabs Max Nightriver's arm, the grip like iron. His eyes are empty, and he doesn't make a sound.

Belle's axe Cleaver comes down in a sudden, crushing arc. The sand erupts in a spray of stone-grey grit, and the sound is like a hammer meeting a wall.

messages.text: Hianxo rises from the harbour in red lacquer and cedar roofs. The letter from Jiansho Academy has brought your party across the Jehopa Ocean for a tournament group entry, but it says little about who asked for you. messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Honami, who asked for us, and why us?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. *She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

The monk's legs are swept from under him, and he hits the sand with a heavy thud, his head still held high as Belle's hammer brings him down into the dirt.
The blade is at his throat, and the monk doesn't blink, doesn't move, doesn't speak. His eyes are fixed on the sky above the ring, and he doesn't acknowledge the blade pressing against his skin.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Honami, who asked for us, and why us?

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"That's a thoughtful question, Darling." Honami's tails swish behind her, one brushing the sleeve of Max Nightriver's robe. "The Academy's administration decided it would be a wise investment to seek fresh perspectives from abroad." She tilts her head, white hair shifting. "A group of foreigners to shake up the tournament—it's been so dull lately, and everyone knows each other's techniques so well. Besides, you were all recommended so highly."
*She leads the way forward, red eyes sparkling as she passes by a tea merchant's stall.*
"Perhaps we should begin with something more tea, yes? A nice walk through the city towards the Academy would be much more refreshing than discussing bureaucracy. You have so far to walk, and I simply can't have you arrive tired."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.text: We sign under Honami's name. Where do we fight?

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"Where you fight?" She smiles sweetly, her fingers trailing along the spine of the book. "That's quite simple. You fight in the tournament grounds, of course. The first round is fought in the sparring courtyards, which are just across the way."
*She points with a slender finger toward a section of the courtyard filled with training equipment and weapons racks.*
"The second round is fought in the central arena, and the final... as you've heard, is fought before the Emperor in the Imperial Palace."
*Her eyes flick toward Honami, and then back to Max Nightriver.*
"You'll find your first-round opponents and your opponents for each round listed on the notice board. It updates every day, so do keep an eye on it. Are there any other questions you have before we get started?"

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"Huh? You want me to go first?" *Belle stops dead, her hand tightening on Cleaver's leather grip.* "You sure you don't want to let some fancy-pants cultivator show how it's done, Nightriver?"
*Her gaze flickers to Honami for a moment before settling back on Max, brown eyes searching. Then she laughs, a short, sharp sound.*
"Alright. If that's what you want." *She heaves her axe over her shoulder, the massive stone head catching the midday sun.* "I'll show this fire-shitter what happens when you try to burn a Mountain-born."
*She starts walking toward the sparring courts, each footfall heavy and deliberate.* "Don't go and lose your head while I'm having a bit of fun."

*His eyes are already scanning the courtyard, taking in every detail—the students, the instructors, the sparring rings, the way the air feels just before a fight.* "I'll keep a lookout from here, and let you know if anything interesting happens."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"Where you fight?" She smiles sweetly, her fingers trailing along the spine of the book. "That's quite simple. You fight in the tournament grounds, of course. The first round is fought in the sparring courtyards, which are just across the way."
*She points with a slender finger toward a section of the courtyard filled with training equipment and weapons racks.*
"The second round is fought in the central arena, and the final... as you've heard, is fought before the Emperor in the Imperial Palace."
*Her eyes flick toward Honami, and then back to Max Nightriver.*
"You'll find your first-round opponents and your opponents for each round listed on the notice board. It updates every day, so do keep an eye on it. Are there any other questions you have before we get started?"

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"Huh? You want me to go first?" *Belle stops dead, her hand tightening on Cleaver's leather grip.* "You sure you don't want to let some fancy-pants cultivator show how it's done, Nightriver?"
*Her gaze flickers to Honami for a moment before settling back on Max, brown eyes searching. Then she laughs, a short, sharp sound.*
"Alright. If that's what you want." *She heaves her axe over her shoulder, the massive stone head catching the midday sun.* "I'll show this fire-shitter what happens when you try to burn a Mountain-born."
*She starts walking toward the sparring courts, each footfall heavy and deliberate.* "Don't go and lose your head while I'm having a bit of fun."

*He finds a clear spot on a raised stone ledge, far from the main crowd but with a perfect view of the fighting ring.* "Here, this is a good vantage point." *He says softly as he leads the party toward the ledge.*

messages.text: I close the distance and drive my shoulder into the left monk's guard, trying to shove him toward the ring edge.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The left monk takes Max Nightriver's shoulder with a sharp exhale, feet skidding back through the raked sand. He doesn't go down; instead, he twists and grabs Max Nightriver's arm, the grip like iron. His eyes are empty, and he doesn't make a sound.
The right monk is already moving—a low, sweeping kick meant to catch Max Nightriver's ankle and throw them off balance. The big monk doesn't rush in, just watches with a calm that feels dangerous.
Belle's axe Cleaver comes down in a sudden, crushing arc. The sand erupts in a spray of stone-grey grit, and the sound is like a hammer meeting a wall.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Read us the rules first, Council Head. Then we'll decide.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
"A wise decision," she says with a smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes. She opens the register and begins to read, her voice clear and measured. "The Jiansho Tournament: Bouts end in submission, knockout, or ring-out. Ring-out is a victory if a contestant leaves the designated combat area. Submission is when a contestant can no longer continue the fight, or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements. Death is regretted and not punished." Her pause is brief, and her smile falters for a fraction of a second. "This year, the final is fought before the Emperor himself, and the winner will receive a prize from his hand. No one will regret thetournament this year."
*She looks up from the register, her blue eyes fixed on Max Nightriver.* "Shall we sign now?"

messages.text: We signed the register, all three of us, so we're in. Belle, you take the first bout against Chen Wei.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"Huh? You want me to go first?" *Belle stops dead, her hand tightening on Cleaver's leather grip.* "You sure you don't want to let some fancy-pants cultivator show how it's done, Nightriver?"
*Her gaze flickers to Honami for a moment before settling back on Max, brown eyes searching. Then she laughs, a short, sharp sound.*
"Alright. If that's what you want." *She heaves her axe over her shoulder, the massive stone head catching the midday sun.* "I'll show this fire-shitter what happens when you try to burn a Mountain-born."
*She starts walking toward the sparring courts, each footfall heavy and deliberate.* "Don't go and lose your head while I'm having a bit of fun."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We follow Belle to the sparring courts. Dalan, find us a spot where you can see the whole ring.

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
"Yes, Captain." *Dalan nods and scans the area, his green-hooded capelet fluttering as he weaves through the students.*
*He finds a clear spot on a raised stone ledge, far from the main crowd but with a perfect view of the fighting ring.* "Here, this is a good vantage point." *He says softly as he leads the party toward the ledge.*
*His eyes are already scanning the courtyard, taking in every detail—the students, the instructors, the sparring rings, the way the air feels just before a fight.* "I'll keep a lookout from here, and let you know if anything interesting happens."

messages.text:
*Belle stops at the edge of the sparring ring, her hand resting on Cleaver's grip.*
"Tch. Let's see if this Chen Wei can actually fight, or if he's just another pompous blowhard." *She spits on the ground and narrows her eyes at the students and instructors who gather around the ring.*
*She scans the crowd, looking for Chen Wei or any other student who looks like they could be worth her time.* "Anyone here gonna step up, or am I just gonna be standing around like a decorative pot?"
*The students whisper among themselves, their eyes wide as they take in the towering woman with the massive axe.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Into the ring, then. Honami, cover us from range. Belle, take the big monk. I'll go for the one on the left.

messages.name: Honami
messages.text:
"Understood, Darling." Honami's white tails swish behind her as she steps to the edge of the ring, red eyes sharp. "I'll cover you both from range."
*She raises a hand, a faint glow of red light beginning to form around her fingertips.* "Stay safe."
*Her tails flick with anticipation, and she doesn't seem to be holding back her power.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: I close the distance and drive my shoulder into the left monk's guard, trying to shove him toward the ring edge.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The left monk takes Max Nightriver's shoulder with a sharp exhale, feet skidding back through the raked sand. He doesn't go down; instead, he twists and grabs Max Nightriver's arm, the grip like iron. His eyes are empty, and he doesn't make a sound.
The right monk is already moving—a low, sweeping kick meant to catch Max Nightriver's ankle and throw them off balance. The big monk doesn't rush in, just watches with a calm that feels dangerous.
Belle's axe Cleaver comes down in a sudden, crushing arc. The sand erupts in a spray of stone-grey grit, and the sound is like a hammer meeting a wall.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
"On it!" *Belle doesn't wait for a second word, and her axe is already moving. She spins in a wide, brutal circle, the head of Cleaver whistling through the air.*
*The big monk moves—a slow, calm sidestep that's almost mocking.* "Fuckin' patience," *she mutters under her breath, and her jaw sets.*
*She steps into the attack, her own weight behind the swing.* "You want to play it safe? Try this!" *she roars, and the axe comes down like a hammer, the sand erupting again in a storm of grey grit.*

messages.text:

"Ring-out," the steward calls, his voice clear. "Left monk of the Mountain Silence—out."
The crowd in the stands is murmuring, and the right monk's expression hasn't changed as he continues to face Max Nightriver and Belle.

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
"Something feels off," *he murmurs, and his fingers close on the bow's string.*
*Dalan is already kneeling on the stone ledge, his eyes scanning the ward-posts and their charms.* "There's a shimmer in the air around the charms, and the onmyoji keeping them look nervous."
*He pulls a long arrow from his pack, his eyes darting to the posts again.* "I'll have you covered from here, if anything tries to get through."
*His eyes are locked onto the ward-posts now, and he's already nocking the arrow, his expression serious.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: I sweep the right monk's leg while Belle hammers his guard down. When he hits the sand I put my blade at his throat. Yield.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
Belle's axe comes down with the weight of a mountain, and the monk's arms rise up to shield his head, his eyes narrowing but his expression remains empty.
The monk's legs are swept from under him, and he hits the sand with a heavy thud, his head still held high as Belle's hammer brings him down into the dirt.
The blade is at his throat, and the monk doesn't blink, doesn't move, doesn't speak. His eyes are fixed on the sky above the ring, and he doesn't acknowledge the blade pressing against his skin.

messages.text: Steward, he can't yield if he won't speak. Call the bout. And Council Head Megumi, how many more rounds before the final bracket?

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
*She doesn't look up from the council box, her eyes fixed on Honami's form below.* "That's right. A bout is won by ring-out or knockout. A contestant who can no longer continue or is unable to fulfill the tournament's requirements is considered to have submitted." *She finally glances at Max Nightriver, and her smile is flawless.* "This is only the first round. There will be six more before the finals."
*She doesn't mention the bout being called, and her eyes drift back to Honami as she makes a note in the register.*

messages.text: Then we fight them all. Over the next days we take every bout in the opening rounds, one after another, until the herald reads out the final bracket.

messages.name: Megumi
messages.text:
*From the high box, she watches the Darrans move from bout to bout, her blue eyes tracking Honami's reactions more than their victories.* "They're moving forward," she murmurs to the empty seat beside her, her voice soft but clear. "And Honami is losing her grip."
*She makes a note in her register, her expression thoughtful as she watches the party win yet another match.*
*The herald's voice rings out across the arena, and Megumi's eyes sharpen as she reads the names on the final bracket.*

messages.text: We listen for our names. Herald, read it again, louder. Are we in the final bracket?

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:

*Honami's white tails swish behind her, and she looks at Max Nightriver with a mixture of pride and worry in her red eyes.* "We've made it to the final bracket, Darling," she says softly, and her tails curl around his arm. "We'll fight in the finals."
*Megumi watches from the council box, and her expression is unreadable as she makes one last note in her register.*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: That night we go back to the empty arena. Dalan, show me what you saw. There's a thread between the ward posts. Honami, can you read the charm on it?

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
*Dalan is already there, standing before the ward-posts, his fingers tracing the air just above the stone.* "Yes, Captain. There's something here, and it's wrong." He points toward the rafters, his eyes narrowed. "A thread, thinner than hair, strung between the posts."
*He pulls a long arrow from his pack and nocks it, his eyes fixed on the thread.* "I couldn't see it from the ledge, but once I got closer, I noticed a shimmer in the light. It's not just silk—it's something else. Something dangerous."
*His eyes flicker to Honami, and he waits for her to respond.* "You can read it, can't you?"

messages.text:
"I can." Honami's white eyes flash as she leans closer to the thread. Her red eyes narrow, scanning the fine strand with her onmyoji's sight. "It's woven with the essence of a spider demon, and coated in poison. The venom is designed to seep into someone's bloodstream the moment they land a strike."
*She runs a finger just above the thread, her expression darkening.* "Whoever set this up intends to kill the opposing fighter in the final bout, right before the eyes of the Emperor. And they want it to look like the Darran entry struck the blow."
*Her tails swish behind her with agitation.* "This is a setup. We're being framed."
